## 10. Chapter 13 & 14 (Virtues & Vices) Decisions

### CH 13 The Virtue-Matrix Ruleset (objective cell test)

A pillar is checked only when it belongs to the virtue's *definition* — what it does by its own nature — not what it merely touches, requires, or receives. Definition test (locked July 2, 2026): **Truth** and **Sacrifice** belong to the definition of *virtue as such* — a virtue is a firm habit of doing good (CCC 1804); the good is what God reveals to be really so, and doing good always gives something away — hence universal in every row, not by design but by definition. **Justice** and **Mercy** appear only in the definitions of particular virtues: Justice (renders something *due* to God or neighbor, including stewardship of one's own body and soul held in covenant trust, 1 Cor 6:19-20); Mercy (*extends* relief beyond what is owed — outward, not received).

**Justice and Mercy are the only discriminating columns.** Faith and Hope receive mercy but never extend it → no Mercy. Hope alone lacks Justice (justice keeps our side of the covenant; hope rests on His — relying is not rendering; Faith's assent is owed to God as First Truth). **Architectonic rule:** Charity, Prudence, Wisdom check all four because their definitions take in the whole of love — charity is love itself; prudence judges what love must do; wisdom sees what love is doing in the whole (this also grounds ch14's Imprudence/Foolishness narrowing). All-four additionally includes the relational six whose defining act is outward mercy (Generosity, Kindness, Patience, Meekness, Gentleness, Zeal).

Applied June 30, 2026: removed Mercy from Hope, Humility, Contentment, Faithfulness, Gratitude, Honesty, Piety, Perseverance, Zeal; §76 recut (Humility dropped from the all-four list). Ruleset also documented in the chapter itself. Ruleset refined July 2, 2026: definition test replaces proper-act wording; Truth/Sacrifice universality grounded in the definition of virtue itself; stewardship clause added to Justice; Hope/Justice recast (relying is not rendering); architectonic three stated definitionally; Sacrifice grounded in self-gift rather than felt cost. Also July 2, 2026: Zeal redefined as zeal for souls (James 5:20) → Mercy added; relational five becomes six. "Defining act" column added to the matrix so each row's marks are read from its stated definition. Primary-pillar stars added under the differentia test (primary = the pillar the defining act cannot be stated without); Charity alone carries four stars. Judgment calls locked: Hope→Sacrifice, Temperance→Sacrifice, Patience→Sacrifice, Contentment→Justice, Zeal→Mercy. Four families result: Truth (Faith, Prudence, Humility, Honesty, Wisdom); Justice (Justice, Chastity, Diligence, Contentment, Obedience, Faithfulness, Gratitude, Piety); Mercy (Generosity, Kindness, Meekness, Gentleness, Zeal); Sacrifice (Hope, Fortitude, Temperance, Patience, Perseverance). Family-list prose upgraded to a four-column table + mirror prose (strong column = open door, avoided column = where to knock; foreshadows the four-saints doors passage). Main matrix unchanged — derivation stays in canonical order; families are the finding; Charity heads no column.

### CH 13 Cut "Integration of Faith and Love" to virtue-as-mechanism only (2026-07-08)

**Why:** Patrick flagged the section (via review comment) as repetitive and off-topic for a chapter about virtues. On inspection this held up: the section was re-arguing that faith without works is dead — ground the book has already covered, and covered better, elsewhere. The Galatians 5:6 "faith working through love" exposition and the closed-fist/four-saints-doors/*incurvatus in se* sanctification passage both duplicate Ch. 9's own "Faith Working Through Love" section, which already runs the open-hand/closed-fist image at length (the ch13 copy was a thinner variant of an image ch9 already owns). The John 3:16-21 light/darkness "believing = doing" argument duplicates Ch. 17 (the Gospel chapter) almost verbatim, including the same "verses often left out" framing move — that argument belongs to the Gospel chapter, not the virtues chapter. None of this content was doing virtue-specific work; it was general soteriology standing in the way of the chapter's actual job. Patrick's direction: assume the reader is already thoroughly convinced faith alone is dead, and keep only what shows the virtues as the practical, concrete *mechanism* by which faith works through love.

**What changed:** the "Justification: Being Made Right with God" subsection went from ~2,500 words to ~430. Cut entirely: the father/addicted-son parable, both 1 Timothy passages (1:3-5, 1:18-19), the "not saved by anything we earn" paragraph, the James 2:19 demons paragraph, the Matthew 25 sheep-and-goats paragraph, the John 3:16-21 passage, and the four-saints/four-doors/*incurvatus in se* passage (reverses the June 28, 2026 graft recorded above — the "foreshadows the four-saints doors passage" line in that entry is now a dangling reference). Kept: the justice/justification etymology (trimmed, with the Council of Trent quote as the anchor — justification as real transformation, not mere declaration, is the distinctively Catholic point and isn't made elsewhere in the book); the fear-of-the-Lord virtue list (Humility, Religion, Obedience, Temperance, Penance, Fortitude, Perseverance); the Prudence/Wisdom growth paragraph; and the Matt 5:48/*teleios* paragraph pointing back to Ch. 10 (already correct practice — a two-sentence pointer, not a re-exposition). Heading changed from "Justification: Being Made Right with God" to "Virtue: How Faith Works Through Love."

### CH 14 The Vice-Matrix Mirror (and its two exceptions)

The vice matrix mirrors the ch13 virtue matrix: a vice offends exactly the pillars its opposing virtue upholds, because vice is the privation of virtue. Truth and Sacrifice offended universally; Justice universally except Despair/Presumption (mirrors Hope); Mercy is the discriminator — offended only when the vice's proper act turns against the neighbor.

Two principled breaks from the mirror, both from reading what the vice-term actually denotes: **Pride** keeps all four though Humility lacks Mercy — as the root sin it destroys the humility mercy flows from (mercy becomes impossible or arbitrary), so the vice is *wider* than its virtue. **Imprudence** and **Foolishness** drop Mercy though Prudence/Wisdom carry it — the virtue-names denote the summit of right judgment while the vice-names denote ordinary lapses, not the total collapse that would reach mercy, so the vice is *narrower* than its virtue. Neither break reopens ch13.

Applied July 1, 2026: removed Mercy from Despair/Presumption, Gluttony, Infidelity/Betrayal, Ingratitude, Dishonesty/Lying, Impiety/Irreverence, Inconstancy/Fickleness, Lukewarmness, Imprudence/Rashness, Foolishness; added Sacrifice to Imprudence/Rashness and Injustice; realigned Lust and Lying prose. All-four vices: Hatred, Pride, Greed, Wrath, Envy, Harshness/Cruelty, Violence.

July 2, 2026: definition test extended to ch14; the mirror demoted from rule to finding — each vice read from its own defining offense. "Defining offense" column and primary-target stars added; Hatred alone carries four stars. Lukewarmness resolved: Truth★, no Mercy (a community can stay big on mercy while going cold on truth — mercy present but unguided; tradition left unnamed per standing rule). Violence set Justice★ (force seizing what was never ours), distinguishing it from Harshness/Cruelty at Mercy★. Wrath Sacrifice★ per the chapter's own "perversion of sacrifice" line. Pride and Imprudence/Foolishness exceptions retained.
